doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

title: Did the women's quintet share that feeling
summary: She did, but the band never discussed it; there was little awareness then.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: When you did this [holds up LP] this is now tempus fugit — this was 24 years ago I think. And I’m wondering if you and your bandmates — did any of them have that same feeling like here’s a quintet of women and we need to prove that we are really good at this?

I cannot speak for the others, I certainly did, and we didn’t talk about any of this at that time. There was really no, or very, very little awareness of that in the scene. This has really, really changed now. Everything’s become a lot more open and people talk about it. But at the time I felt the only way to prove my worth or to — you know it’s terrible to talk in those terms but this really was what I felt and I know a lot of other women felt that too was by playing in a certain way that shows yeah, she can do it too, she can play or you can sound like a guy. But as far as the others at the time I don’t really know. My hunch is yes but see the fact that we didn’t even talk about any of this — amongst women! You know? There was so much unconscious stuff that I didn’t understand until much, much later.
